chunks.content: ## Adjusting Clothing Distortion and Deformation in CLO This section explains how to identify and correct twisted garment deformation caused by errors in sewing lines using CLO's 2D and 3D windows and editing tools. Key terms include sewing line adjustment, Edit Sewing Line Tool, Swap Sewing Line, and garment simulation. ### Identifying Twisted Deformation in Garments Twisted deformation in garments during simulation typically results from incorrect sewing lines. These sewing lines represent how fabric panels are connected, and errors in their direction or position cause the clothing to twist unnaturally in 3D simulation. To detect these errors: - Load the garment file (e.g., "Fixing Deformation of the Garment") into the 2D or 3D window. - Observe the simulation for twisted or distorted areas. - Note that because fabric panels in the 2D window are flat, it can be difficult to visually pinpoint sewing line errors without assistance. ### Using the Edit Sewing Line Tool to Locate Errors CLO provides the **Edit Sewing Line Tool** in the 3D toolbar to help identify problematic sewing lines: - Select the tool. - In the 3D view, left-click on the twisted area of the garment. - The corresponding sewing line will be highlighted in the 2D window. This allows you to correlate twisted deformation in 3D with specific sewing lines in 2D, enabling precise corrections. ### Correcting Sewing Line Direction with Swap Sewing Line A common cause of twisting is sewing lines with inconsistent direction or cross-sections: - Right-click on the identified faulty sewing line in the 2D window. - From the context menu, select **Swap Sewing Line**. - This action reverses the sewing line's direction, aligning it properly with the counterpart panel. After swapping, activate the garment simulation to check if the twisting is resolved. Rotate the 3D view as needed to inspect the garment from different angles, especially the back view where distortions may be more visible. ### Adjusting Sewing Line Position for Deformation Fix If swapping the sewing line direction does not fully correct the deformation, the position of the sewing line itself may be incorrect: - With the **Edit Sewing Line Tool** active, select and move the sewing line along the panel outline in the 2D window to a more accurate position. - This adjustment realigns the sewing curve, reducing twisting in the 3D garment simulation. After repositioning, run the simulation again to observe the effect. Repeat this process iteratively until the garment returns to a natural, untwisted state. ### Summary of Procedure 1. Load garment file into CLO's 2D and 3D windows. 2. Identify twisted areas in the 3D simulation. 3. Use **Edit Sewing Line Tool** to select sewing lines causing deformation. 4. Swap sewing line direction if inconsistent. 5. Adjust sewing line position along panel outlines if needed. 6. Re-run the simulation and inspect results. 7. Repeat adjustments until deformation is corrected. --- This methodical approach to correcting sewing line errors ensures accurate garment simulation and reduces distortion, improving the realism and quality of the final virtual clothing.
